title: The Trigger Isn't a Revenue Number. It's a Question You Can No Longer Answer Alone.
linkedin:
Plenty of owner-led businesses set themselves a number. Once revenue hits five million, or ten, that's when a fractional CFO gets a seat at the table.

It's a tidy plan, and it's almost always measuring the wrong thing.

Here's what we see across owner-led businesses instead. Two businesses turning over six million dollars a year can sit in completely different places. One sells a single product through one bank facility. The other runs three revenue lines, a working capital facility with covenants attached, and a partner asking sharper questions every quarter.

Same number on the top line. A very different amount of financial judgement required to run it well.

The real trigger isn't a milestone on the P&L. It's a moment when the owner realises they're the only person in the business who can answer a particular financial question, and answering it alone is starting to cost more than it should.

Three signals tend to matter more than any revenue figure: every meaningful financial call running through one person with nobody to pressure test it, complexity quietly outgrowing the reporting, and an outside party, a bank, an investor, a buyer, asking a question that takes days to answer instead of minutes.

None of these show up on an income statement. That's exactly why the revenue number feels like the easier thing to wait for.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog. Link in the first comment.
